texts.paragraph: The honey badger ranges across sub-Saharan Africa and southwest Asia, occupying burrows it digs with long foreclaws. It feeds opportunistically on insects, scorpions, reptiles, birds, and mammals, and is notorious for raiding beehives. Despite its small size it confronts lions and buffalo when cornered, relying on thick loose skin and a fierce temperament rather than speed.
